title: Conformalized Link Prediction on Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: GNN applications in high-stakes domains are hindered by unreliable predictions, while existing uncertainty quantification methods often lack rigorous uncertainty estimates.

gap.claim: It is unclear whether conformal prediction's exchangeability assumption holds for dependent graph data in link prediction, and whether the resulting prediction sets or intervals can be sufficiently efficient.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces a distribution-free, model-agnostic uncertainty quantification approach for constructing predictive intervals for GNN-based link prediction.
The authors establish a permutation-invariance condition for applying conformal prediction to link prediction and report exact test-time coverage.
The paper develops a sampling-based method that aligns graph structure with a power-law distribution prior to standard conformal prediction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe this work as the first attempt to introduce a distribution-free and model-agnostic uncertainty quantification approach for GNN-based link prediction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments achieve the desired marginal coverage and significantly improve conformal prediction efficiency compared with baseline methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Unreliable GNN predictions limit use in high-stakes domains, and existing uncertainty methods may lack rigor.
The work proposes conformalized link prediction, based on conformal prediction, for distribution-free uncertainty quantification.
The approach must address exchangeability under dependent graph data and achieve useful prediction-set or interval efficiency.
The authors establish a permutation-invariance condition and connect graph power-law adherence with conformal prediction efficiency, then introduce a sampling-based alignment method.
Experiments are reported to achieve marginal coverage while improving efficiency relative to baselines.

source_observation.claim: For dependent graph data, the paper addresses conformal prediction validity through a permutation-invariance condition and addresses efficiency through graph-structure-aware sampling.

interpretation.claim: When applying distribution-free uncertainty methods to structured data, validity assumptions and output efficiency may require separate, structure-aware treatment.

application.claim: For other structured prediction settings, explicitly test the method's statistical assumptions and use domain structure to reduce inefficient prediction sets or intervals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these conditions or efficiency improvements generalize beyond GNN-based link prediction.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact permutation-invariance condition.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baseline identities, numerical coverage values, or efficiency measurements.
The abstract does not describe the sampling algorithm's implementation details or computational cost.
